title: Run throwaway helper calls with --bare and --no-session-persistence
source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference — `--bare` (skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP, auto memory, CLAUDE.md) and `--no-session-persistence` (print mode, non-resumable)
description: The small Haiku helper calls — _call_helper_json (delegate.py:1498/1508), the routing/triage call (delegate.py:2042), the session summariser (session.py:335) and explain.py:341 — are one-shot classifiers. Today each one boots a full Claude Code session: it discovers and loads the operator's global CLAUDE.md, every skill and plugin, every user-scope MCP server, and auto-memory, then persists a session record. That is seconds of startup and a large multiple of the actual task's tokens per call, on calls that run many times per sprint, and it makes classifier output sensitive to unrelated global config. --bare plus --no-session-persistence makes them hermetic, fast and reproducible.
proposed_changes: 1) Add `_helper_cmd(model, prompt, *, json_out=True) -> list[str]` in delegate.py that builds `[claude, -p, --model, <resolved>, --bare, --no-session-persistence, (--output-format json), --, prompt]`, gating --bare and --no-session-persistence on capability probes so older CLIs degrade to today's argv. 2) Replace the four hand-built argv lists (delegate.py:1498, :1508, :2042, session.py:335, explain.py:341) with calls to it. 3) IMPORTANT: do not use --bare for real delegations — Morty runs need MCP, subagents and skills; keep it strictly on the helper path, and add a comment saying so. 4) Log the wall-clock of helper calls to the daily jsonl before/after so the latency win is measurable. 5) Add a regression test asserting no helper argv contains --mcp-config and every delegation argv still does.
